items.title: Paquito D'Rivera — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I regret that I never have the chance to go abroad to study... with Marseille Muir. But that was not possible

ctx.x: What was it like at the conservatory?

The life at the conservatory in some ways good. Private teaching is fine, but the life of the school is always recommendable because you have relations with all of the students, you know, you can compare yourselves with, you learn to share your life with others, you develop private jokes with others. Is always important the life of the conservatory, and I regret that I never have the chance to go abroad to study, but we have what my father have in mind—and still I have the letter—is to go to study a couple of…
Let’s go back to your formal education. Talk about going to school and the schools you went to, other than the conservatory.
